newsitem.title: USA: Numbers to direct Wall Street opening.
newsitem.headline: Numbers to direct Wall Street opening.

text.p: U.S. stocks, fresh from a sharp rally, are expected to make their starting move Wednesday based on economic data out before the markets' opening, analysts said.
Investors will take their cue from preliminary figures for the U.S. first quarter real gross domestic product (GDP). Due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, they can provide early warning of higher interest rates.
"After yesterday's strong rally, obviously the market again will be directed by this morning's economic news," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia investments.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 179.01 points to close Tuesday at 6962.03, the second-biggest point gain in its history. Investors were buoyed by data that pointed to reduced inflation.
The average forecast for the quarter's GDP calls for a 4.1 percent rise, against 3.8 percent for the last quarter of 1996. The deflator is 1.7 percent, against 1.5 percent for the previous period.
Markets also will be looking at the Chicago purchasing management index for April, out at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. The average forecast is for 56.2 against 57.5 for March.
Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, called for a slightly higher opening on a follow-through from Tuesday's rise.
Tuesday's "market was a rebirth of irrational exuberance," he said.
However, Cardillo predicted a slight dip at the start on profit-taking.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei average rose 480.75 points, or 2.57 percent, to end at 19,151.2, its best close since Dec 30.
In London, the FTSE 100 was down 1.8 at 4431.4. U.S. shares were mixed to lower on profit-taking following New York's big jump.
The dollar was steady in Asia and in Europe was trading at 1.7270/75 against the mark.
The Standard & Poors 500 futures index was off 0.45 to 799.35. The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was off 7/32 to yield seven percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said Goldman Sachs had started a list of stocks for bargain hunters. They include Intel Corp, Citicorp, Safeway Inc and Anadarko Petroleum Corp.

The New York Times' Market Place column reported mutual fund investors continued to temper their enthusiasm for domestic stock funds in April. This month more money went into international stock funds than those that invest in domestic shares.
